subject: Clarification: subprocessor evidence & international transfer posture for Acme Health
messages:

Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: subprocessor evidence + transfer mechanisms

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our vendor intake we need a compact packet on two items before Legal advances the DPA: 1) an export of the current subprocessor list (including regions where subprocessors process data), and 2) a clear statement of transfer mechanisms you rely on for cross-border processing (SCCs, BCRs, or adequacy).

Specifically Acme needs: 
- CSV manifest with subprocessor name, function, country, and whether they store or merely transit PII.
- Any attestations you can share about KMS custody for customer data and whether RSA/PKI keys leave the US.
- If you rely on SCCs, a note about which template/version and whether you apply Supplementary Measures.

We try to keep requests tight — a single-sheet matrix plus references is ideal. Can you share by EOD Tue so legal can review ahead of our vendor committee on Fri?

Appreciate it,
Alan

--

Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor evidence + transfer mechanisms

Hi Alan — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Marissa (Privacy Ops) and Karthik (Platform Security) to assemble the packet.

Quick answers up front:
- We'll provide a subprocessor manifest as a CSV with country + processing purpose.
- Cross-border transfers: hosted data for US customers is served from US regions by default; for EU customers we can pin to EU regions. We rely primarily on the EU SCCs (2021/2021 variants where applicable) plus targeted supplementary measures (encryption at rest with customer KMS options).
- KMS custody: we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) in Dedicated/Private; for hosted customers we use KMS services — key material for hosted customers is kept in region-bound KMS unless customer requests export for dedicated arrangements.

Marissa/Karthik — can you confirm the CSV export and attach the transfer matrix? Also flag any subprocessors that only transit tokens vs. store PII. Alan — I'll try to get the packet to you by EOD Tue but may be Wed morning depending on legal evidence pulls.

Thanks,
Hannah

Hi all — attaching the requested artifacts. See inline for quick clarifications.

[Attachment: subprocessor_manifest.csv (CSV) — columns: name,function,country,stores_pii,notes]
[Attachment: redwood-transfer-matrix-2027-04.pdf (PDF) — summary of transfer mechanisms per region]

Key notes: 
- Subprocessors that only provide CDN/transit do not retain customer prompt/response payloads per our retention policy; those rows are marked "transit_only".
- For hosted customers without CMK, KMS keys are region-bound and managed by cloud provider; we do not export key material outside the specified region.
- We use the EU SCCs (version 2021, Commission Implementing Decision) as our baseline for EEA transfers. For specific regulated customers (healthcare, finance) we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment so that keys and storage remain under customer control.
- Supplementary measures: encryption-in-transit (TLS1.3), organizational controls (contractual audit rights), and technical segregation for high-risk customers.

Alan — if Legal wants a short excerpt of the DPA clause that references SCC application and how we implement supplementary measures, I can pull the approved language and include it.

-Marissa

1) Can you confirm whether any of the subprocessors listed have access to raw prompts or outputs for debugging? If yes, which ones and what is the access justification?
2) For the rows marked "transit_only" — can you add a short note explaining the technical boundary (e.g., TLS termination, no persistence beyond ephemeral caches)?

If you can drop those two clarifications by EOD Thu we should be able to close the vendor package before our committee. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
